comment: The missed mechanism was architecture before activation: on a 1.5-turn spiral with weak plain-SGD progress, residual depth (and stable early normalization) controls boundary expressivity. Thus the five-block residual GELU C edges the otherwise identical leaky E; the four-block residual SiLU D beats the shallower three-block ReLU B; the deep non-residual A remains last. I over-applied K1008/K1039's rectifier tendency and K1066's “more LN” rule, neither of which isolates this low-Delta SGD regime.
hypothesis: A scoped rule is: for 1–2-turn spirals trained with plain SGD at lr around 3e-4 and T around 2k, rank residual MLPs primarily by depth when LN counts are comparable; among equal-depth deep residuals, prefer an input-normalized smooth activation (GELU) over a leaky rectifier whose first block is unnormalized; rank non-residual stacks last despite depth. Mechanism: residual composition preserves a usable signal while each added block supplies another boundary-warping stage; early LN stabilizes the weak-SGD regime. This predicts C>E>D>B>A. A history check over six comparable low-rate spiral rankings gave four exact pairwise/order matches and two misses, so this is a useful local heuristic, not a universal law.
